lines.text: Sarah wants eggs next Friday. On signet, that's a futures contract — a Cashu future.
Each production day is its own series. The unit names the farm, the commodity, and the maturity. Friday's eggs are not Saturday's eggs.
The terms are a small signed document, and its SHA-256 digest is its address. Every proof's secret carries one tag pointing at it.
Sarah picks a production day. Five eggs, twenty-one sats each.
One hundred and five sats. A real Lightning invoice on signet.
Paid. The mint issues exactly five claims, locked to Sarah's wallet key.
Five bearer claims — the details show the unit, the terms digest, and the maturity.
The farm's ledger counts totals only. A claim beyond capacity simply cannot be minted.
Sarah gives Bob two of her notes. Not a payment — a handover, like cash.
Here's what she hands him: the mint, the unit, and two proofs — Sarah's proofs.
Bob's wallet takes them straight to the mint and swaps them: Sarah's notes are burned.
The mint issues fresh proofs of the same future — same unit, same terms tag, but brand-new secrets. Only Bob's keys can spend them now.
Sarah keeps three. The farm's ledger never moved.
Friday, four p.m. — the series matures. For the film, we advance the clock with the admin override.
Bob redeems two at the counter. The wallet burns the proofs and shows the teller a code.
The operator matches the code, hands over two eggs, and settles. Until that moment, nothing is consumed.
Redeemed. The spent proofs can never be spent again.
Signet sats in. Dated bearer claims out. Hand to hand, no registry. Physical redemption at maturity.
NUT-32, draft one — live on signet, enforced by the mint, and checked end to end by automated tests.
